title: MATH GAOKAO - 403
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Translating verbal constraints into a system of inequalities
questions.learningObjective: Build a system of inequalities from a production limit and a minimum production requirement.
questions.question: A workshop makes \(x\) chairs and \(y\) tables. It can make at most \(40\) items per day, and it must make at least \(10\) chairs. Which system of inequalities represents these constraints? Assume \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers.
questions.explanation:
The phrase “at most \(40\) items per day” means the total number of chairs and tables cannot exceed \(40\), so \(x+y \le 40\). The phrase “at least \(10\) chairs” means \(x \ge 10\). Since the numbers of chairs and tables cannot be negative, \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). Therefore, the correct system is \[
x+y \le 40,\ x \ge 10,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Translate each phrase involving “at most” or “at least” into an inequality before combining the conditions.

questions.concept: Modeling a budget constraint and a minimum purchase condition
questions.learningObjective: Form a system of inequalities from a spending limit and a minimum quantity requirement.
questions.question: A student buys \(x\) notebooks at \(3\text{ USD}\) each and \(y\) pens at \(2\text{ USD}\) each. The total spending cannot exceed \(30\text{ USD}\), and the student must buy at least \(4\) notebooks. Which system of inequalities models this situation? Assume \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers.
questions.explanation:
The cost of \(x\) notebooks is \(3x\), and the cost of \(y\) pens is \(2y\). Since total spending cannot exceed \(30\text{ USD}\), \(3x+2y \le 30\). The student must buy at least \(4\) notebooks, so \(x \ge 4\). The numbers of notebooks and pens cannot be negative, so \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). Hence the correct system is \[
3x+2y \le 30,\ x \ge 4,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: First express the total cost, then compare it with the given spending limit using the correct inequality sign.

questions.concept: Building nutrient constraints from minimum requirements
questions.learningObjective: Construct inequalities representing minimum nutritional requirements in a diet problem.
questions.question: Each serving of food A contains \(2\) units of protein and \(1\) unit of iron. Each serving of food B contains \(1\) unit of protein and \(3\) units of iron. A meal must provide at least \(8\) units of protein and at least \(9\) units of iron. Let \(x\) be the number of servings of food A and \(y\) be the number of servings of food B. Which system of inequalities models the requirements?
questions.explanation:
Food A contributes \(2x\) units of protein, and food B contributes \(y\) units, so the protein requirement is \(2x+y \ge 8\). Food A contributes \(x\) units of iron, and food B contributes \(3y\) units, so the iron requirement is \(x+3y \ge 9\). Since servings cannot be negative, \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). Therefore, the correct system is \[
2x+y \ge 8,\ x+3y \ge 9,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Write one inequality for protein and one inequality for iron, using “at least” for each minimum requirement.

questions.concept: Modeling time limits and a ratio constraint
questions.learningObjective: Translate a maximum total time and a minimum ratio condition into inequalities.
questions.question: A student plans to spend \(x\) hours studying mathematics and \(y\) hours studying physics. The total study time cannot exceed \(6\) hours. The time spent on mathematics must be at least twice the time spent on physics. Also, at least \(1\) hour must be spent on mathematics. Which system of inequalities represents these conditions?
questions.explanation:
“Total study time cannot exceed \(6\) hours” gives \(x+y \le 6\). “Mathematics time must be at least twice physics time” gives \(x \ge 2y\). “At least \(1\) hour must be spent on mathematics” gives \(x \ge 1\). Also, time cannot be negative, so \(y \ge 0\). Thus the correct system is \[
x+y \le 6,\ x \ge 2y,\ x \ge 1,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Identify the maximum condition and the minimum condition separately, then translate “at least twice” into an inequality.

questions.learningObjective: Form inequalities from a maximum perimeter and a minimum length-width relationship.
questions.question: A rectangular garden has length \(L\) and width \(W\). Its perimeter must be at most \(100\) meters, and its length must be at least \(5\) meters more than its width. Which system of inequalities models these constraints?
questions.explanation: The perimeter of a rectangle is \(2(L+W)\). Since the perimeter must be at most \(100\), we have \(2(L+W) \le 100\). The length must be at least \(5\) meters more than the width, so \(L \ge W+5\). The dimensions must be positive, so \(L>0\) and \(W>0\). Therefore, the correct system is \(2(L+W) \le 100,\ L \ge W+5,\ L>0,\ W>0\).
questions.hint: Recall the perimeter formula for a rectangle, and translate “at least \(5\) more than” into an inequality.

questions.concept: Modeling weight capacity and minimum box quantities
questions.learningObjective: Build inequalities from a maximum carrying capacity and lower bounds on quantities.
questions.question: A delivery truck can carry at most \(1200\text{ kg}\). A box of type A weighs \(30\text{ kg}\), and a box of type B weighs \(40\text{ kg}\). The truck must carry at least \(10\) boxes of type A and at least \(5\) boxes of type B. Let \(x\) be the number of type A boxes and \(y\) be the number of type B boxes. Which system of inequalities models this situation? Assume \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers.
questions.explanation:
The total weight is \(30x+40y\). Since the truck can carry at most \(1200\text{ kg}\), \(30x+40y \le 1200\). The truck must carry at least \(10\) type A boxes, so \(x \ge 10\), and at least \(5\) type B boxes, so \(y \ge 5\). Also \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). Hence the correct system is \[
30x+40y \le 1200,\ x \ge 10,\ y \ge 5,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Compute the total weight first, then apply the capacity limit and the minimum box requirements.

questions.learningObjective: Construct a system of inequalities from minimum machine hours and maximum raw material.
questions.question: A factory produces \(x\) units of product A and \(y\) units of product B. Product A uses \(2\) machine-hours and \(1\text{ kg}\) of raw material per unit. Product B uses \(1\) machine-hour and \(3\text{ kg}\) of raw material per unit. The factory must use at least \(20\) machine-hours and can use at most \(30\text{ kg}\) of raw material. Which system of inequalities models these constraints? Assume \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers.
questions.explanation:
The total machine-hours are \(2x+y\), and this must be at least \(20\), so \(2x+y \ge 20\). The total raw material used is \(x+3y\), and this can be at most \(30\), so \(x+3y \le 30\). Production quantities cannot be negative, so \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). Therefore, the correct system is \[
2x+y \ge 20,\ x+3y \le 30,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Write separate expressions for total machine-hours and total raw material, then attach the correct inequality direction to each.

questions.concept: Modeling investment limits and a proportional restriction
questions.learningObjective: Translate total investment, minimum allocation, and ratio conditions into inequalities.
questions.question: An investor puts \(x\text{ USD}\) into bond A and \(y\text{ USD}\) into bond B. The total investment cannot exceed \(10000\text{ USD}\). At least \(3000\text{ USD}\) must be invested in bond A. The amount invested in bond B must be no more than twice the amount invested in bond A. Which system of inequalities represents these constraints?
questions.explanation:
“Total investment cannot exceed \(10000\)” gives \(x+y \le 10000\). “At least \(3000\) in bond A” gives \(x \ge 3000\). “Bond B must be no more than twice bond A” gives \(y \le 2x\). Investment amounts cannot be negative, so \(x \ge 0\) and \(y \ge 0\). Thus the correct system is \[
x+y \le 10000,\ x \ge 3000,\ y \le 2x,\ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Translate “no more than twice” carefully: the quantity that is limited must be on the left side of the inequality.

questions.concept: Modeling multiple resource limits with minimum production
questions.learningObjective: Build a feasible-region system from egg, flour, and minimum-production constraints.
questions.question: A bakery makes \(x\) cakes and \(y\) pies. Each cake requires \(2\) eggs and \(1\) cup of flour. Each pie requires \(1\) egg and \(2\) cups of flour. The bakery has at most \(20\) eggs and at most \(24\) cups of flour available. It must make at least \(3\) cakes and at least \(2\) pies. Which system of inequalities models these constraints? Assume \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers.
questions.explanation:
The total eggs used are \(2x+y\), and only \(20\) eggs are available, so \(2x+y \le 20\). The total flour used is \(x+2y\), and only \(24\) cups are available, so \(x+2y \le 24\). The minimum production conditions give \(x \ge 3\) and \(y \ge 2\). Therefore, the correct system is \[
2x+y \le 20,\ x+2y \le 24,\ x \ge 3,\ y \ge 2
\].
questions.hint: For each resource, multiply the amount per item by the number of items, then compare the total with the available amount.

questions.concept: Synthesizing multiple constraints into one inequality system
questions.learningObjective: Model a situation involving a minimum difference, a maximum total, and a lower bound.
questions.question: A café sells \(x\) small cups and \(y\) large cups of coffee. The number of small cups sold is at least \(3\) more than twice the number of large cups sold. The total number of cups sold is at most \(15\). At least \(4\) small cups are sold. Which system of inequalities models these conditions? Assume \(x\) and \(y\) are nonnegative integers.
questions.explanation:
“The number of small cups is at least \(3\) more than twice the number of large cups” means \(x \ge 2y+3\). “The total number of cups sold is at most \(15\)” gives \(x+y \le 15\). “At least \(4\) small cups are sold” gives \(x \ge 4\). Since the number of large cups cannot be negative, \(y \ge 0\). Thus the correct system is \[
x \ge 2y+3,\ x+y \le 15,\ x \ge 4,\ y \ge 0
\].
questions.hint: Separate the sentence into three conditions: a minimum difference, a maximum total, and a lower bound on small cups.
